_meta.indication: Indicated in adult and pediatric patients for treatment of inhalational anthrax due to B. anthracis in combination with appropriate antibacterial drugs, and for prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax when alternative therapies are not available or not appropriate.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: NZW rabbit monotherapy treatment Study 1 (16 mg/kg IV vs placebo)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not applicable — efficacy demonstrated in animal models under the Animal Rule; no human efficacy trial / NCT
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled monotherapy treatment study in NZW rabbits challenged with aerosolized B. anthracis spores (Ames strain) and treated after developing systemic anthrax
pivotal_trials.population: New Zealand White rabbits with systemic inhalational anthrax, positive for bacteremia prior to treatment
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of survival at Day 28 (28 days after spore challenge)
pivotal_trials.result: Day 28 survival 93% (13/14) with ANTHIM vs 0% (0/9) placebo; p=0.0010 (95% CI 0.59, 1.00)

key_safety: Safety studied only in 320 healthy volunteers. Hypersensitivity reactions were the most common adverse reactions, occurring in 34/320 (10.6%), with 3 (0.9%) cases of anaphylaxis. Most frequent adverse reactions (single-dose ANTHIM vs placebo) included headache (8% vs 6%), pruritus (4% vs 1%), and upper respiratory tract infections (5% vs 3%).
target_moa: Monoclonal antibody that binds free protective antigen (PA) of B. anthracis toxin (Kd 0.33 nM), inhibiting PA binding to its cellular receptors and preventing intracellular entry of anthrax lethal factor and edema factor; it has no direct antibacterial activity.
modality: mAb (chimeric IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody, ~148 kDa)

boxed_warning.content: Hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis have been reported during IV infusion of ANTHIM; administer in monitored settings by personnel trained and equipped to manage anaphylaxis, monitor closely, and stop infusion immediately if hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis occurs.

rems.type: FDA concluded Anthim can be safely used without restrictions on distribution or use; no REMS was required under the Subpart H approval.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA Advisory Committee because obiltoxaximab has the same target and treatment indications as raxibacumab, the previously approved anti-PA monoclonal antibody; no new questions warranted AC input.

summary.text: Anthim (obiltoxaximab) was approved under 21 CFR 601 Subpart H (Animal Rule), because human efficacy studies are not ethical or feasible; efficacy was established in animal models of inhalational anthrax while safety was evaluated in healthy human volunteers. The product held Fast Track designation (2006) and Orphan Drug Designation (2006), was reviewed as a standard application, and was not referred to an Advisory Committee.
